recipes.name: Chicken Curry Salad in a Hurry
ingredients_raw: 1 rotisserie chicken, meat and skin removed and chopped

steps.text: Mix the chicken, eggs, mayonnaise, apple, celery, onion, curry powder, paprika, cayenne pepper, and salt in a large bowl. Cover and refrigerate for 1 hour before serving.

raw_recipe.headline: Chicken Curry Salad in a Hurry
raw_recipe.description: Rotisserie chickens makes this salad extra easy.
raw_recipe.name: Chicken Curry Salad in a Hurry
recipeIngredient: 1 rotisserie chicken, meat and skin removed and chopped

recipeInstructions.text: Mix the chicken, eggs, mayonnaise, apple, celery, onion, curry powder, paprika, cayenne pepper, and salt in a large bowl. Cover and refrigerate for 1 hour before serving.

review.reviewBody: Easy and delicious! I used a Granny Smith Apple and red onion. I left out the egg and replaced that with a combination of sliced grapes, raisins, and chopped walnuts. I mixed the dressing in a separate bowl before folding it into the chicken and other ingredients. For the dressing I used 1/2 cup of Hellman's light mayo cut with 1/4 cup of reduced fat sour cream for added creaminess along with the curry, paprika and cayenne pepper. I also added a little bit of salt and black pepper. It chilled for just a couple of hours and it came out really good. Overall, a great combination of flavors! Especially good on whole grain bread!

I love this recipe - quick, easy and delicious. I doubled the curry and used 2 pks of Perdue Shortcuts (roasted). Left out the egg and apple, and added 2 tbsp of Mango Chutney for a touch of sweetness. Then, served on sweet rolls with lettuce. Um, Um, Good!

This is a very versatile recipe. You can add any type of nuts or harder fruits to the mayonnaise and it will be delicious. I added pepitas to the mix. I'm also cutting down on very sweet fruit such as raisins so I added about a 1.5 gala apple to replace the raisins. I like more mayo and curry so I added a little extra. It also freezes well.

If you're not used to too much spice, then you'll probably like this. It was okay, but we're used to more flavor in our "curry" chicken salad. I used at least a tablespoon of curry powder and doubled the cayenne. It still needed something, so I added some lime juice, cilantro and dried cranberries. Then it was perfect.

I only had 1/2 a rotisserie chicken -- so cut ingredients in half. It was simply delish and an excellent solution to the leftover chicken. Next time I will add more apple - I used a Granny Smith.

No need to tinker with the ingredients.

I followed the recipe exactly except I used 2 cups shredded chicken breast I had in my freezer. Next time I make this, I will add more apple and less celery just because it’s my preference. The ratio of apple to celery to onion needs to be adjusted for my taste preference. I love the curry and paprika, though!

I love the versatility of this chicken salad!!! 
Absolutely delicious and easy as is! However, at times, I make additions, my favorite being toasted slivered almonds, but other times toasted pecans, if that's what I have on hand. My favorite way to eat it is with tortilla chips or with wheat thins toasted chips. Yum!
Delicious recipe. Can vary to your taste or mood. Added 2 tsp of Curry, salt, pepper, and fresh parsley.
Thanks a lot! It was great and easy. I did not used roasted chicken, but just used a piece of chicken breast. I added raisins to make it pop.
Just made this recipe and it is amazingly tasty!!!! I didn't have apples so I substituted pomegranate instead. I will be making this again, and again, and again!

I was not very impressed with this recipe. Maybe I had an extra large chicken, but the mayonnaise wasn't near enough to cover the pieces (and I don't like things mayonnaisey at all, so I was looking for a very light coating, not a heavy dressing). Even after adding extra mayo, the salad felt like it was missing something. I added in a little honey and a tbsp of chopped pecans and that made it better, but I don't think I'll be making this recipe again. There are some other excellent chicken curry salad recipes available on this site, so I will go back to those next time.

Pretty good! Didn't have a rotisserie chicken so I just boiled and chopped 2 frozen chicken breasts. Probably would have been more flavorful with rotisserie chicken, but it was still tasty this way :)

As I was putting this together and reached for the apple, it was gone. My husband had eaten it an hour earlier. Despite missing the apple, the chicken salad was delicious and I can't wait to make it again with the apple.
I thought this was just okay. I followed the recipe exactly but added grapes. Unremarkable which is odd because I love curry.
What a great recipe! I hate eggs so I threw in some raisins instead. Everyone loves this.

I made it exactly as written and it was fabulous! It's rare to find something this easy to prepare that is a hit with everyone at a gathering, particularly when people are not always fans of curry. It was eaten and I could have made far more, with much praise thrown in from the party-goers. I just brought Vienna buns and some bibb lettuce, than sat back and enjoyed the company. Highly recommend.

I had leftover cooked chicken breast and needed a quick recipe. I skipped the hard boiled eggs and apple. I did have celery. This made a really tasty quick curry sandwich filling. I'll make it again, hopefully when I have an apple around.
light on the curry blends well with fruit

I'm sorry for the average review. I used leftover rotisserie chicken and went exactly by the recipe. I was really hoping to like it with the apple in it, but it was just average. I think it may of been either the cayenne or paprika that threw off the taste for me. I tried to doctor it up to save it. Thanks for the recipe to try! I did enjoy making it.
Will make again. Used two types of curry...one hot, one mild.
